# Investigation: trace of the mission-list sync guard (`compareLedgers`/`countComplete`), issue #1054 corrected scope

## Setup
- Baseline commit: `662bcd33` in worktree `/Volumes/WorkspaceA/ylminiserver/workspace/kaola-workflow/.kw/worktrees/bundle-1054`.
- Worktree tree has uncommitted edits from other agents to `scripts/kaola-workflow-claim.js` / `kaola-workflow-ledger-compare.js` and their plugin mirrors (`git status --short` at start of session showed 8 modified + 2 untracked). All code quoted below was read via `git show 662bcd33:<path>` into `/Volumes/WorkspaceA/ylminiserver/workspace/kaola-workflow/kaola-workflow/bundle-1054/.cache/{claim,ledger-compare,test-ledger-compare}-baseline.js`, never from the dirty working tree.
- Main root `/Volumes/WorkspaceA/ylminiserver/workspace/kaola-workflow` and its `kaola-workflow/archive/` read-only.
- Issue authority: `gh issue view 1054 --json body,comments` (rewritten body + 2026-09-09 09:01:45Z correction comment).

## 1. Call graph

`grep -rn "compareLedgers\|countComplete"` across `scripts/`, `plugins/kaola-workflow/scripts`, `plugins/kaola-workflow-gitlab/scripts`, `plugins/kaola-workflow-gitea/scripts` (all four are byte-identical `kaola-workflow-ledger-compare.js` copies + one claim.js caller per edition):

- **Definition**: `scripts/kaola-workflow-ledger-compare.js` — `countComplete(text)` counts lines matching `/^[ \t]*(?:-[ \t]+)?status:[ \t]*done[ \t]*$/i`; `compareLedgers(srcText, destText)` fails open (`safe:true, reason:'ok'`) when `destText == null || destText === '' || countComplete(destText) === 0`, else refuses (`safe:false, reason:'would_regress_complete_ledger'`) iff `countComplete(destText) > countComplete(srcText)` (strict `>`).
- **Callers, both inside `mirrorFinalizationArtifacts` (write path) and `probeFinalizeMirror` (read-only `--check` prediction), one pair per claim.js edition** (canonical `scripts/kaola-workflow-claim.js:3600/3619`, `plugins/kaola-workflow/scripts/kaola-workflow-claim.js:3600/3619`, GitLab `kaola-gitlab-workflow-claim.js:3397/3416`, Gitea `kaola-gitea-workflow-claim.js:3394/3413`; second call site canonical `:3925/3928`, mirrored per edition). No sink-merge call site: `scripts/kaola-workflow-sink-merge.js` has zero references to `compareLedgers`/`ledger-compare` (grepped `ledger-compare|compareLedgers|pending_mirror|source_dir|main_root` — no hits). The guard is exclusively a finalize-transaction concern.

**`mirrorFinalizationArtifacts(root, project)`** (claim.js:3573-3665, doc comment :3554-3572):
- `mainRoot = realpath(mainRootFromCoord(...))`; if `mainRoot === realpath(root)`, returns `not_needed` (in-place run, no mirror at all).
- `srcDir = mainRoot/kaola-workflow/<project>`, `destDir = root/kaola-workflow/<project>` — **SOURCE is always the main checkout's copy, DEST is always the linked worktree's copy** (`root` here is the worktree the transaction runs in).
- If `destDir` absent AND an archive authority already exists → `skipped_post_archive` (crash-resume; the live folder is gone on purpose).
- If `srcDir` absent → `source_absent`.
- If `srcRecord` (`srcDir/mission-list.md`) exists: reads `destText` (null if unreadable/absent), calls `compareLedgers(srcRecord text, destText)`.
  - **verdict.safe → `ledger_compare: 'pass'`.**
  - **verdict.safe === false (UNSAFE, dest strictly more "done" than source)**: the transaction "owns the repair" (#837) — `mergeCopyDir(destDir, srcDir, null, FINALIZE_MIRROR_TREE_BOUND)`, i.e. **copies the WORKTREE (dest) UP into MAIN (src)**, "worktree wins," skipping only the two tree-bound artifacts (`.cache/chain-receipt.json`, `.cache/<outcome-log>`, kept whichever side already has them). Re-runs `compareLedgers` against the now-repaired `srcRecord`. If the merge threw, or the re-compare is still unsafe, returns `{ refused: true, inner_reason: 'mirror_sync_failed', detail: ... }` — **fail-closed, zero-write on the worktree side** (nothing has been copied into the worktree yet at that point). On success, `ledger_compare: 'synced_from_worktree'`.
  - If `compareLedgers` itself throws a non-`TypeError`/`ReferenceError` (e.g. require failure) → `ledger_compare: 'skipped_no_script'` (fails open, does not block).
  - If `srcRecord` absent → `ledger_compare: 'skipped_no_record'`.
- Final step, unconditional once the guard clears: `mergeCopyDir(srcDir, destDir, FINALIZE_MIRROR_DEST_OWNED, FINALIZE_MIRROR_TREE_BOUND)` — **copies MAIN (src) DOWN into the WORKTREE (dest)**, skipping `workflow-state.md`/`workflow-tasks.json` when dest already owns one, and skipping the two tree-bound artifacts either direction.

**`probeFinalizeMirror(root, project)`** (claim.js:3915-3945ish) mirrors the same branch order **read-only**, for `finalize --check`. It reports `state: 'ready'` (mirror will run and construct the authority) or `'sync_required'`/`'sync_failed'` (UNSAFE verdict; writable → machinery-repairable, so it's a *state*, not a *reason* the operator must act on) or `'source_absent'`/`'skipped_post_archive'`. `destAuthorityAbsent` is a separate bit ("dest has no `workflow-state.md` yet") used by the caller to know the mirror will *construct* the authority. `resolveFinalizeAuthority`/the authority-topology builder (claim.js ~4073-4083) emits the exact shape the task description quotes: `{ main_root, linked_root, source: 'pending_mirror'|'live'|'archive'|'none', source_dir, dest_dir }`, where `source_dir` = the main copy, `dest_dir` = the worktree copy, and `source: 'pending_mirror'` fires whenever Step 8a hasn't run yet and will construct the authority (this is the *directory*-absent/first-sync case, not specifically tied to a `compareLedgers` verdict).

**When dest is absent (first sync)**: `compareLedgers` never even reaches its content comparison — `destText == null` short-circuits to `safe:true`. **When dest is identical / repeat execution**: not specially cased; if `countComplete` on both sides is equal, `destComplete > sourceComplete` is false → `safe:true` regardless of whether the bytes are literally identical.

## 2. The historical regression it guards

Origin commit `58ffd812` ("enhancement(finalize/init): contractor Step-8a ledger-regression guard ... (#399,#410)", 2026-06-11): the **original** guard counted `| <id> | complete |` rows in a **`## Node Ledger` table inside `workflow-plan.md`** (a different file, a different record, from the pre-Mission-List era), with this header comment (verbatim):

> "The Step-8a mirror `cp -R`s `kaola-workflow/{project}/.` from the main checkout into the linked worktree right before archive. Run from the WRONG direction (cwd = main checkout with a staler main copy), it clobbers a finished run's worktree ledger — resetting `complete` rows to `pending` so the archive commits a pending-ledger plan (the 2026-06-11 audit reproduced this live at v5.14.0/ba094a2)."

CHANGELOG (`4907:`, same date) confirms: "The 2026-06-11 full-workflow audit reproduced live (at v5.14.0/ba094a2) a clobber where the contractor's Step-8a artifact mirror `cp -R`'d a STALER main `kaola-workflow/{project}/` over a finished worktree copy, resetting its `## Node Ledger` from `complete` back to `pending` so the archive would commit a pending-ledger plan."

**Direction of the incident**: main→worktree `cp -R`, executed from the wrong cwd/direction, overwrote a *worktree* copy that had progressed further with a *staler main* copy — i.e. the copy the guard exists to refuse is precisely the routine main→worktree Step-8a direction when main is behind.

**Re-point to the Mission List**: commit `c0b48043` ("docs(claude): rewrite CLAUDE.md onto the mission list; remove the banner", 2026-07-31) changed `countComplete`/`compareLedgers` from the `## Node Ledger` table parse to the current `status: done` line-regex over `mission-list.md`, with the comment "THE PROPERTY IS THE POINT, NOT ITS DERIVATION... What changed is only what it counts." Test coverage for this re-point was accidentally dropped and restored by `34ce2d60` ("test(ledger-compare): restore the anti-clobber fence coverage over mission-list records ... Found by the PR #879 review" — that PR belongs to the #877 mission-list extraction campaign, `git log --grep=877` shows `814e9eaf`/`b3bc7acf` etc. as that campaign's commits). `8e42a864` (issue #837, same era) is the ladder-subtraction commit that made the worktree→main "repair" (`mergeCopyDir` + re-compare + `mirror_sync_failed`) part of the transaction itself instead of an operator-typed refusal — it did not touch `ledger-compare.js`'s content logic.

`git log -S'compareLedgers' --oneline` — 17 touching commits total; the file-content history (`--follow`) is exactly `58ffd812` (create) → `63443589` (fold into cmdFinalize, #816) → `c0b48043` (re-point to mission-list, quoted above). No commit since has changed `countComplete`'s regex or `compareLedgers`'s strict-`>`/fail-open logic.

**Stale documentation found in the process**: `docs/decisions/D-777-01.md` (v7.0.0-era ADR) still says *"ledger-compare is positional, so a column before status silently disables `would_regress_complete_ledger` with no error"* — that sentence describes the **pre-`c0b48043` positional `## Node Ledger` table parser**, not the current line-regex-over-mission-list implementation, which is not positional at all. This is a documentation drift the corrected scope's item 4 should account for if D-777-01 is touched, but it is not this issue's guard code.

## 3. Existing tests

- **`scripts/test-ledger-compare.js`** (baseline, 188 lines, its own header says "re-pointed at the MISSION LIST by #877"): pins `countComplete` against the documented `record()` fixture format (H1 + `- item:` bullets, 2-space-indented fields) and 8 accepted hand-edited indent/case variants + 7 rejected non-matches; one "KNOWN COARSENESS" pin (`status: done` embedded inside a multi-line `result: |` block over-counts — accepted as tolerable because the miscount is symmetric on both sides of a strict-`>` comparison). Covers `compareLedgers`: (a) staler-source-vs-more-done-dest → UNSAFE; (b) dest absent/empty/zero-done → SAFE (first sync, three sub-cases); (c) source ≥ dest, **including the exact-equal-count case** → SAFE ("an idempotent mirror re-run is never refused"); (d) both empty → SAFE. Plus CLI exit-code coverage (0/3/1) and `--help`. **Everything in this suite is written in LINE-FORM only** (its `record()` helper only emits `- item:`/`  status:` bullets) — **no scenario constructs a table-form (`| item | status | ... |`) record**, so the file-format blindness measured in §4 below has no existing regression coverage.
- **`scripts/test-finalize-door.js`**: integration-level, drives the real `claim.js finalize --keep-worktree` CLI over fixture worktrees. `T12_refusalNamesTheGiveTheClaimBackRoute`'s `finalize_mirror_refused` door builds a real worktree with `mission-list.md` = 3 done rows and a **read-only, unwritable** main copy with `mission-list.md` = 1 done row (also line-form via the same `missionList()` helper) — asserts the CLI actually returns `reason: 'finalize_mirror_refused', inner_reason: 'mirror_sync_failed'` end-to-end when the repair cannot write. `T10_mirrorPreservesTreeBoundArtifacts` covers the sibling guarantee (chain receipts/outcome logs are never clobbered by either mirror direction) but does not exercise `compareLedgers` itself. Neither this file nor `T8m`'s `pending_mirror` topology assertion (line 1446) constructs a table-form record.
- **`scripts/test-forge-finalize-findings.js`**: grepped for `ledger`/`mirror`/SAFE/UNSAFE/`compareLedgers` — no hits scoped to this guard (its "mirror" hits are the retired ROADMAP.md generated-mirror, unrelated).
- **Coverage gap, stated plainly**: first-sync ✓, repeat/equal-count ✓ (but not literal byte-identity, and not table-form), staler-dest-vs-fresher-source (the routine safe direction) ✓ for line-form, real regression (staler-source-vs-more-done-dest) ✓ for line-form including an end-to-end fail-closed CLI proof. **Not covered anywhere in the shipped baseline test suite: any table-form fixture, any scenario with equal counts but different content (the exact false-safe hole #1054 is about), and any scenario distinguishing "genuinely no work done yet" from "work done but uncounted."**
  - Note: the uncommitted `scripts/test-issue-1054-mission-list-carriers.js` (another agent's in-flight work, not part of the baseline `662bcd33` and explicitly out of scope for me to read as shipped) does add table-form E1-E5 assertions per the pre-correction remedy — its E4/E5 pin exactly the count-equality behavior the corrected scope withdraws as the fix shape, so it should not be treated as authoritative for this trace.

## 4. Real behavior now (baseline `662bcd33`, run against real files)

Ran `node -e` against `git show 662bcd33:scripts/kaola-workflow-ledger-compare.js`'s exported `countComplete`/`compareLedgers`, over real files under the main root:

**(a) `countComplete` on real archives** — census: 68 line-form archives, 5 table-form, 3 other (of 76 total under `kaola-workflow/archive/`; `issue-1050` turned out to be table-form too, so the line-form fixture used was `kaola-workflow/archive/bundle-1001-1002/mission-list.md`).

| Fixture | Form | `countComplete` |
|---|---|---|
| `kaola-workflow/archive/bundle-1053/mission-list.md` (7 `\| done \|` rows, all real finished work) | table | **0** |
| `kaola-workflow/archive/bundle-1001-1002/mission-list.md` | line | **10** |

**(b) `compareLedgers(tableA-with-3-rows-removed AS SOURCE, tableA AS DEST)`** — removed the last 3 of 6 data rows from the real bundle-1053 table to construct a source that is genuinely, unambiguously less complete than the dest:
```
{"safe":true,"reason":"ok","sourceComplete":0,"destComplete":0}
```
**The guard reports SAFE on a copy that would erase 3 of 7 finished rows**, because both sides count 0 under the line-regex. This reproduces the false-safe hole against real production data, not a synthetic fixture.

**(c) `compareLedgers(lineA-with-one-done-turned-todo AS SOURCE, lineA AS DEST)`** — flipped one `status: done` to `status: todo` in the real line-form archive:
```
{"safe":false,"reason":"would_regress_complete_ledger","sourceComplete":9,"destComplete":10}
```
Correctly UNSAFE — the line-form path works as designed on real data.

**(d) The actual #1053 finalize.** `kaola-workflow/archive/bundle-1053/finalization-summary.md`'s `## Mission List` section reads `items: 0`, `carrying an outcome while their status is not done: 0` — **but that is `probeMissionListCoherence`'s output** (the finalize-summary auto-statistics scope item 1 of #1054 removes), **not `compareLedgers`'s verdict**; the two are separate probes over the same file and must not be conflated. I found **no artifact in `kaola-workflow/archive/bundle-1053/.cache/**` or the chain receipt that records `ledger_compare`'s literal token** for that run — `mirrorFinalizationArtifacts`'s return value is not persisted anywhere the archive kept. What I can state directly: `countComplete` on the real, final, table-form record is measured at 0 (§4a), so *had* the guard's content-comparison arm been reached during that run, it would necessarily have read `sourceComplete: 0` on whichever side was table-form. Whether that run's mirror actually took the `destText == null` (dest-absent, first-sync) branch or the `countComplete(destText) === 0` branch of the fail-open `if` (claim.js:3600-3606 `if (destText == null || destText === '' || countComplete(destText) === 0)`) is **not distinguishable from the archived evidence** — both return `ledger_compare: 'pass'` with identical shape. **Inference, not measured**: given the run record shows dispatch/evidence paths rooted at the MAIN copy (`kaola-workflow/bundle-1053/.cache/...`, no `.kw/worktrees/` prefix) while code changes were committed on the worktree branch, the coordination record's live authority for this run plausibly lived in **main**, not the worktree — which is the opposite of the guard's design assumption (§5, D-423-01/comment at claim.js:3554 "the worktree holds the complete ledger and the main copy is the one carrying the Finalization artifacts"). Confidence: medium; refuted by direct evidence of the worktree's own `mission-list.md` state pre-mirror, which no longer exists (the worktree was removed post-sink).
**What `ledger_compare: pass` means when both sides count 0, stated precisely**: it means "the fail-open first-sync arm fired" — it carries **zero information about whether the destination actually held finished, uncounted work**, because the same return shape (`safe:true, reason:'ok', sourceComplete:0, destComplete:0`) is produced whether the destination is genuinely empty (legitimate first sync — the case the fail-open exists for) or genuinely holds a complete table-form record the parser cannot see (the false-safe case reproduced in §4b). The guard cannot and does not distinguish these two.

## 5. Proposal (non-binding, minimal, mine to describe — not to implement)

Per the corrected scope: protect by content, direction, and authority; no counts; no new parser/state system; do not delete protection; reuse existing diff/coordination.

**Candidates evaluated**, each against the two real copy directions in §1 (main→worktree "Step 8a mirror," and the #837 repair's worktree→main "sync") and the three ADR-0017 write moments (create; in-place status-word mutation on dispatch; in-place status+result mutation, or a wholly new row, on completion):

1. **Byte-identical → safe.** Zero false-safe risk (trivially correct — no bytes lost). Exactly covers the pinned "repeat execution / idempotent re-run" scenario (§3's `(c)` equal-count case, now proven at the byte level instead of the count level). No false-refusal risk of its own. **Recommended, as one arm of the rule, not the whole rule** — real repeat-executions (finalize `--check` then finalize, or a crash-resume re-entry) should be byte-identical, so this alone handles that case without ever looking at content shape.
2. **Dest absent/empty → safe (first sync).** Same as today; unambiguous (nothing exists to lose). No behavior change needed here — this arm is already layout-agnostic and already correct. **Keep unchanged.**
3. **"Dest content entirely contained in source" (line-set or prefix containment) → safe.** Evaluated against the write model: because `status:` (and a table row's status cell) changes **in place** — the old line/row literally disappears and a different-valued line/row appears at the same position — neither a line-*set* containment test nor a byte-*prefix* test reliably holds even for the ordinary, legitimate "source has progressed further than dest" case (the exact case this arm is meant to safely pass). It only reliably fires for the narrower case where growth is *purely appending new rows/blocks* with zero in-place mutation of prior lines — real Mission Lists routinely violate that (status advances in place at every write moment). **False-safe risk**: low by construction (it never claims safety unless a strict textual containment check passes) — but the more permissive a containment definition is made to reduce false refusals (e.g. per-line set instead of ordered prefix, or fuzzy matching), the closer it gets to re-deriving field semantics, which is exactly the coupling the corrected scope forbids. **False-refusal risk**: high — it will *not* fire on the single most common legitimate case (in-place status advance), so it buys little over arm 1 in practice while adding line/row-splitting logic that starts to look like a parser. **Not recommended** as currently specifiable without semantic parsing; flag for the orchestrator rather than silently trust.
4. **Otherwise → refuse fail-closed** (report both paths + a diff summary), Main Orchestrator reconciles. **False-safe risk: none** (this is the fail-closed default). **False-refusal risk: high relative to today's guard** — any divergence at all (including a legitimate one-sided main→worktree copy of genuinely-ahead content) now stops the mirror and requires an orchestrator round-trip, where today's count-based guard would have silently passed. This is the direct trade the corrected scope asks for ("safety never judged by counts") — it converts every *possible* content loss into a surfaced question instead of a silent guess, at the cost of surfacing some *safe* copies too.

**Recommendation**: arms 1 + 2 unchanged/tightened-to-bytes, plus arm 4 as the fail-closed default — **drop arm 3** (containment) as unable to meet its own bar given the in-place mutation write model, unless a future measurement shows the false-refusal rate from arms-1/2/4-alone is high enough in practice to justify accepting arm 3's narrower, honest "byte-prefix-only" form (which would at least never manufacture a false safety claim, only a missed opportunity to skip an orchestrator round-trip). For the diff summary, reuse the codebase's existing idiom rather than inventing one: `scripts/kaola-workflow-claim.js` and `kaola-workflow-sink-merge.js` already shell `git diff`/`diff` via `execFileSync` at ~10 call sites for exactly this kind of "report what changed" duty (e.g. `claim.js:411`, `:3698`, `:3792`; `sink-merge.js:316`, `:662`) — a plain `diff -u <dest> <src>` (or `git diff --no-index` if a `diff` binary cannot be assumed) truncated the same way other refusal details already are (`.slice(0, 400)` pattern at claim.js:3625/3663) is the minimal, already-idiomatic choice; no new dependency, no new state file.

**On the `mergeCopyDir(... worktree wins)` repair, directly answering the question asked**: yes, as currently written it **can** overwrite a newer main-side record. The repair's premise (claim.js:3554-3558, doc comment) is an unconditional assumption — *"the worktree holds the complete ledger and the main copy is the one carrying the Finalization artifacts the orchestrator just authored"* — baked in as a fixed direction (`mergeCopyDir(destDir, srcDir, ...)`, worktree→main, always) whenever `compareLedgers` reports UNSAFE, with **no check of which side is actually authoritative**. §4d's inference is that #1053's authoritative coordination record plausibly lived in **main** (dispatch/evidence paths rooted there), which is the reverse of that assumption; had that run also hit the UNSAFE branch (it evidently did not — it hit the fail-open pending_mirror/first-sync arm instead), the repair would have pushed a worktree copy up over a main copy that was, in that run's actual topology, the more current one. Switching the guard from counts to content-diff (recommendation above) does not by itself fix this: a byte-diff refusal still needs *something* to decide "worktree wins" versus "ask the orchestrator," and the current code hardcodes the former unconditionally. Given the corrected scope's own framing — "the Main Orchestrator reads the raw record and the actual evidence and writes its conclusion" — the more consistent minimal change is to **retire the automatic worktree-wins repair** for the content-divergent case and let refusal arm 4 route straight to the orchestrator (which already owns exactly this judgment per scope item 1), rather than have the machinery guess a direction that #1053 shows is not universally true. Confidence: medium-high on the structural claim (the direction is unconditionally hardcoded, verified by reading claim.js:3609 directly); lower on whether #1053 specifically would have hit this branch (see §4d's stated inference/confidence).
